objections.claim: The startup no-listener guarantee is unsound for the native launcher. Its source review and environment clearing begin only after process startup, but a normally dynamically linked launcher may execute attacker-selected code through LD_PRELOAD, LD_AUDIT, or another dynamic-loader surface before main() clears anything; a library constructor can call socket/bind/listen first. The approach neither requires a static loader-independent launcher nor verifies the packaged executable has no interpreter, shared-library closure, dynamic loading, inline-syscall, or assembly escape. The NODE_OPTIONS and SIGUSR1 fixtures therefore do not discriminate this bypass. Qualification must enforce and inspect a hermetic launcher binary/loader closure and include a preload-constructor listener regression.

Open-hash-fexecve of the same file descriptor does not provide the claimed mutation-point content binding for node, git, gh, or bwrap. An open descriptor pins an inode, not immutable bytes; another writer can modify that inode after hashing, close its write descriptor, and leave fexecve to execute the changed contents through the original descriptor. This defeats the stated same-path adversary without changing the path or reported version. The runner must execute an immutable snapshot, such as a verified copy in a sealed executable memfd, or prove equivalent kernel-backed immutability, and qualification needs an in-place-overwrite-after-hash regression.
